intro: In English, people often use one word, kung fu, for every Chinese martial art. In China the picture is much wider. There are northern and southern systems, family styles named for villages and teachers, temple stories, national programs, and a modern sport with two separate rule books.

In this unit you will visit real places: the Shaolin Monastery in Henan, Chen Village, a Shanghai club founded in 1910 and a national institute in Nanjing. You will also meet the films that made some of these names famous around the world, from Hong Kong studios to American television.

By the end, you will be able to name the words Chinese speakers use for martial arts. You will tell a legend from a record, and taolu from sanda. You will also be able to check a school's name by asking for its place, its teachers, its governing body and its papers.
bigQuestion: How do we find the real places, people and rule books behind the one English word kung fu?

timeline.t: The Shaolin Monastery is founded on Mount Song in Henan
A Shaolin stele records monks helping Li Shimin in 621
The Yijin Jing appears, later tied to the Bodhidharma legend
The Jingwu Athletic Association is founded in Shanghai
The Central Guoshu Institute opens in Nanjing
The Chinese Wushu Association is founded
Bruce Lee names Jeet Kune Do; the Ving Tsun Athletic Association forms
Fist of Fury opens; the TV series Kung Fu begins on ABC
The film Shaolin Temple draws crowds to Dengfeng
The International Wushu Federation is founded
UNESCO lists taijiquan as intangible cultural heritage

words.d: the Mandarin word for martial arts; also a modern sport with judged routines and bouts
skill built through long effort; the source of the English word kung fu
national art; the Republican government's name for martial arts in the 1920s and 1930s
a set routine performed alone and scored by judges
a modern wushu bout sport held on a raised platform, also called sanshou
a carved stone slab with writing that records an event
a story about the past that records cannot prove
a line of teachers and students that passes an art down
a person whose story grows larger as people retell it
a community living far from its homeland, and keeping ties to it
a document that creates an organization and states its purpose
a document or object made at the time being studied

test.q: Which English word comes from gongfu?
test.why: Kung fu is an older spelling of gongfu, skill built through effort.

test.q: Which province is home to both Shaolin and Chen Village?
test.why: Shaolin on Mount Song and Chenjiagou are both in Henan Province.

test.q: What did the Central Guoshu Institute try to do?
choices: make martial arts a national program
test.why: Founded in Nanjing in 1928, it organized martial arts as a national program.
The International Wushu Federation, founded in 1990, runs world wushu.

test.q: What kind of evidence is the stele of 728?
test.why: A stele is a stone slab with writing; this one records the monks' help in 621.

choices: by the length of the film
by the size of the school
test.why: Taolu is judged on quality, performance and difficulty, like figure skating.

test.q: Which of these is a legend, not a record?
choices: Ip Man's move to Hong Kong
test.why: Records tying Zhang Sanfeng to taijiquan appear centuries later, so historians label it a legend.

test.q: Which region gave many southern styles their Cantonese names?
test.why: Southern styles such as Hung Gar and Wing Chun come from Guangdong, where Cantonese is spoken.

test.q: Who was a real teacher of Wing Chun in Hong Kong?
test.why: Ip Man taught Wing Chun in Hong Kong from the early 1950s.

test.q: What does the duan wei system give?
test.why: The Chinese Wushu Association created duan wei ranks in the late 1990s.

test.q: Why did Jingwu matter in history?
choices: It was a public club open beyond one family
test.why: Founded in 1910, Jingwu taught many styles in a public club.

test.q: What do sanda athletes compete on?
choices: a stage in a film studio
a raised platform called a leitai
test.why: Sanda bouts take place on a raised square platform called a leitai.

test.q: Which law ended U.S. immigration quotas based on national origin?
choices: the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965
test.why: The Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965 ended national-origin quotas.

test.q: What is the best way to check a school's name?
choices: compare it with records such as charters and certificates
test.why: A historian checks a school's claim against its place, teachers, governing body and papers.

test.q: What is a film best evidence of?
choices: the time and place that made it
test.why: A film is a primary source for its makers and audience, even when its story is invented.

write.prompt: Is the English word kung fu a good name for Chinese martial arts? Argue your answer. Cite at least three dated records from this unit, such as the 728 Shaolin stele, Jingwu's 1910 founding, the 1928 Guoshu Institute or the 1990 IWUF, and one film.
tips: Name each record and give its date.
Label legends as legends and records as records.
Compare taolu and sanda using the unit's terms.
Say what a film tells about its own time, not about a school's founding.
